lessons.unit: Spring 1: Money; multiplication and division begins
lessons.title: Bridge: tens and ones to 100
lessons.bigQuestion: What does each digit in a 2-digit number tell us?
objectives: Make 2-digit numbers from tens and ones
Say the value of each digit
successCriteria: All: make a number with Lego tens and ones
Most: say the value of each digit
Some: show the same number with 0 ones or many ones
lessons.crossCurricular: Everyday life: packs of 10 in shops
lessons.smsc: Social: working in teams of ten

keywords.def: one of 0 to 9 in a number

hook.text: Which does NOT show 46?
hook.a: Begin with bismillah (بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ). 6 tens and 4 ones is 64.

teach.heading: Build it
teach.note: Hold up Lego. Ask: how many towers? (3) How many ones? (5).

teach.heading: Place value chart
teach.note: Point to columns. Ask: in 72, what is the 7 worth? (70).

teach.heading: Zero holds the place

misconception.right: 4 tens and 0 ones is 40: the 0 holds the ones place

teach.note: Ask: what is 4 tens and 0 ones? (40).

check.why: The 5 is in the tens place, so 50.

independent.a: 4 tens 7 ones; 7 tens 4 ones; 7 tens 0 ones

independent.q: Extend: what is the 3 worth in 37 and in 73?

exit.q: 8 tens and 1 one = ?
Big question: in 64, what does each digit tell us?

lessons.homework: Make three 2-digit numbers with Lego or pasta in tens and say the tens and ones.
lessons.send: SEND: use real objects and a number line, one step at a time. EAL: picture cards for key words. Stretch: show 45 in two ways.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Money; multiplication and division begins
lessons.title: Bridge: numbers to 100 in words; partitioning
lessons.bigQuestion: How many ways can we split a 2-digit number?
objectives: Read and write numbers to 100 in numerals and words
Partition into tens and ones, and in other ways
successCriteria: All: write a number in words
Most: partition into tens and ones
Some: partition in more than one way
lessons.crossCurricular: English: spelling number words with hyphens
lessons.smsc: Moral: sharing a whole in different ways

hook.text: 56 = 50 + 6. Can 56 also be 40 + 16? Prove it with Lego.
hook.a: Begin with bismillah (بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ). Yes: 40 + 16 = 56. We can partition flexibly.

teach.heading: Number words
bullets: forty-six: tens word, hyphen, ones word
teach.note: Note 'forty' has no u. Ask: write 83 in words. (eighty-three).

independent.q: Core: partition 29, 64 and 50 into tens and ones.
Stretch: write three ways to partition 48.

exit.q: Write 'sixty-eight' in digits.
Big question: give two ways to split 35.

lessons.homework: Write your door number (or any number to 100) in words and partition it two ways.
lessons.send: SEND: use real objects and a number line, one step at a time. EAL: picture cards for key words. Stretch: write all the tens words from ten to one hundred.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Money; multiplication and division begins
lessons.title: Bridge: compare and order numbers to 100
lessons.bigQuestion: How do we decide which number is greater?
objectives: Compare numbers to 100 with <, > and =
Order numbers smallest to greatest
successCriteria: All: compare by tens
Most: compare when the tens are the same by looking at ones
Some: order four numbers and explain
lessons.crossCurricular: Science: comparing heights of plants
lessons.smsc: Moral: we do not boast about having more

keywords.def: put in a line by size

hook.text: Which is greater: 38 or 83? Same digits! How can you tell?
hook.a: Begin with bismillah (بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ). 83: 8 tens beats 3 tens.

independent.q: Stretch: 4_ > 47. What digits could go in the gap?

exit.q: Big question: how do you compare 64 and 69?
exit.a: Same tens, so compare ones: 9 > 4, so 69 > 64

lessons.homework: Find four 2-digit numbers at home (on packets or clocks) and order them.
lessons.send: SEND: use real objects and a number line, one step at a time. EAL: picture cards for key words. Stretch: order five numbers greatest first.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Money; multiplication and division begins
lessons.title: Bridge: count to 100 forwards and backwards
lessons.bigQuestion: How can counting in groups make counting quicker?
objectives: Count to 100 forwards and backwards from any number
Count in 2s, 5s and 10s
successCriteria: All: count on and back in ones across a ten
Most: count in 2s, 5s and 10s from 0
Some: count in 10s from any number, such as 23, 33, 43
lessons.crossCurricular: Qur'an: counting the ayat of a surah
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: the blessings of Allah are too many to count

keywords.def: a number in a counting pattern, like 5, 10, 15

hook.text: There are 40 dates on a tray. Is it quicker to count them in 1s or in 10s?
hook.a: Begin with bismillah (بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ). In 10s: 4 jumps instead of 40.

teach.heading: Across a ten
bullets: After 9 ones comes a new ten.
teach.note: Count aloud together. Ask: what comes after 69? (70). Before 50? (49).

teach.heading: Count in 10s
bullets: The ones digit stays the same.

teach.heading: Count in 2s and 5s
teach.note: Say the pattern together as a spoken chant. Ask: what do you notice about the ones in the 5s? (5 or 0).

check.why: Take 1 ten each time: 55. 64 takes away 1.

independent.q: Stretch: count in 10s from 6 to 96. How many jumps?

exit.q: What comes before 70?
Big question: count 30 pasta in 10s and in 2s. Which is quicker?

lessons.homework: Count in 2s, 5s and 10s to 100 with a grown-up as a spoken chant, 5 minutes a day.
lessons.send: SEND: use real objects and a number line, one step at a time. EAL: picture cards for key words. Stretch: count in 3s to 30.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Place value to 100
lessons.title: Number lines to 100
objectives: Place numbers on a number line from 0 to 100
Estimate the position of a number

keywords.def: make a sensible guess close to the real answer
in the middle between two numbers

teach.heading: A 0 to 100 line
teach.note: Draw the line with tens marked. Ask where 50 is and why. Note that 0 to 100 line is not the same as 0 to 10 scaled up.

teach.heading: Find 37
bullets: Place it just before the middle.
teach.note: Show how to find a number between two marked tens. Teach: first the tens, then the ones.

teach.heading: Estimate
bullets: An estimate does not need to be exact.
teach.note: Show a number line with an arrow pointing between marks. Children say the number that the arrow is closest to.

teach.heading: Halfway numbers
teach.note: Use the idea of halfway to place and round. Ask: how did you work it out?

practice: Where is 70 on a 0 to 100 line?
What number is halfway between 40 and 60?
independent: Draw a number line 0 to 100 and mark 25, 50, 75.
An arrow points between 60 and 70, near 70. Name a number it could be.
Estimate: where is 91 on the number line?
exit: What number is halfway between 10 and 30?
lessons.homework: Draw a 0 to 100 number line with a ruler. Mark 10 numbers of your choice.
lessons.send: SEND: use a pre-marked line. Stretch: number lines 0 to 1000 with marks at hundreds.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Money; multiplication and division begins
lessons.title: Bridge: bonds to 10 and 20; related facts
lessons.bigQuestion: If we know one fact, how many more facts do we know?
objectives: Recall bonds to 10 and 20
Use a bond to find related facts
successCriteria: All: recall bonds to 10
Most: use 6 + 4 = 10 to find 16 + 4 = 20 and 60 + 40 = 100
Some: write the whole fact family
lessons.crossCurricular: Everyday life: making 20p with coins
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: knowledge grows from what we know

keywords.def: two numbers that make a total
a fact linked to one we know

hook.text: 7 + 3 = 10. Use it to find 17 + 3, 70 + 30 and 10 - 3. How many facts can you make?
hook.a: Begin with bismillah (بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ). 20, 100, 7, and more: one fact unlocks many.

independent.q: Extend: write the fact family for 12, 8, 20.

exit.q: Big question: from 2 + 8 = 10 write two more facts.

lessons.homework: Bond of the week: bonds to 20 and tens to 100, 5 minutes a day.
lessons.send: SEND: use real objects and a number line, one step at a time. EAL: picture cards for key words. Stretch: bonds to 50 in tens and fives.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Money; multiplication and division begins
lessons.title: Bridge: add and subtract ones to a 2-digit number
lessons.bigQuestion: What changes when we add ones to a 2-digit number?
objectives: Add and subtract a 1-digit number to and from a 2-digit number
Cross a ten using a bond
successCriteria: All: add ones without crossing a ten
Most: add by making the next ten
Some: subtract ones across a ten
lessons.crossCurricular: Everyday life: adding more stickers
lessons.smsc: Moral: patience; step by step

keywords.def: the ten we reach next, like 40 after 38
jump to a ten, then on

hook.text: 34 + 5 is easy. Why is 38 + 5 trickier?
hook.a: Begin with bismillah (بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ). 38 + 5 crosses a ten: 38 + 2 = 40, then + 3 = 43.

exit.q: Big question: how do you add 47 + 6?

lessons.homework: Use your 100 square: 5 additions crossing a ten (like 37 + 5) with a grown-up.
lessons.send: SEND: use real objects and a number line, one step at a time. EAL: picture cards for key words. Stretch: add three 1-digit numbers to a 2-digit number.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Addition
lessons.title: Adding across the next ten
objectives: Add ones by making the next ten
Use bonds to bridge ten

keywords.def: go across a ten by splitting the number to add

starter: How many more to get from 38 to 40?

teach.heading: Make the next ten
teach.note: Show a number line from 37 to 40 to 42. Explain why we split the 5.

teach.heading: Finish the sum
teach.note: Write the steps. Ask: why did we choose to split 5 into 3 and 2?

teach.heading: Another example
teach.note: Children identify the bond to the next ten (8 and 2), then the remaining 4.

teach.heading: Check with ten frames
teach.note: Use a ten frame picture to visualise making ten and the leftover. Connect to partitioning.

practice: What do you add to 69 to get to 70?
independent: Show 45 + 8 on a number line.
Write a rule to explain how to add across a ten.
exit: Show how you made the next ten.
lessons.homework: Solve eight sums that cross a ten and show your bridging steps.
lessons.send: SEND: use ten frames. Stretch: add 2-digit numbers using bridging in tens.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Money; multiplication and division begins
lessons.title: Bridge: add and subtract tens
lessons.bigQuestion: What happens to the digits when we add a ten?
objectives: Add and subtract multiples of 10 to and from a 2-digit number
Spot that only the tens digit changes
successCriteria: All: find 10 more and 10 less
Most: add and subtract 20, 30 or 40
Some: explain why the ones digit stays the same
lessons.crossCurricular: Everyday life: 10p coins
lessons.smsc: Social: helping others step by step

hook.text: 45, 55, 65, 75. What is happening? What comes next?
hook.a: Begin with bismillah (بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ). Adding 10 each time; next is 85.

exit.q: Big question: why does 36 + 20 still end in 6?
exit.a: We added tens, not ones, so the ones digit stays

lessons.homework: Start at your age and count on in 10s to over 90; then back.
lessons.send: SEND: use real objects and a number line, one step at a time. EAL: picture cards for key words. Stretch: add 19 by adding 20 and taking 1.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Addition
lessons.title: Adding two 2-digit numbers
objectives: Add two 2-digit numbers by adding the tens and ones
Use a partitioning method

keywords.def: writing numbers one under the other, ones under ones

teach.heading: Add tens, add ones
teach.note: Show partitioning of both numbers. Add the tens then the ones, then recombine.

teach.heading: Using rods and cubes
teach.note: Use base ten or a picture. Ask children to explain what each group is.

teach.heading: Column method
bullets: Add the ones first, then the tens.
teach.note: Introduce the layout. Emphasise lining up ones under ones. Sort out misalignments.

teach.heading: Practise
teach.note: Children choose partitioning or columns. Review answers: 57, 69, 89.

independent: A shop has 35 red apples and 42 green apples. How many altogether?
Make up a 2-digit addition with the answer 79.
lessons.homework: Solve six 2-digit additions (with no crossing of ten in the ones) and check each with a different method.
lessons.send: SEND: use place value counters in a column grid. Stretch: add three 2-digit numbers.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Addition
lessons.title: Adding with exchange
objectives: Add two 2-digit numbers when the ones make 10 or more
Exchange ten ones for one ten

keywords.def: swap ten ones for one ten (or ten tens for one hundred)
move the new ten into the tens column

starter: How many ones make one ten?

teach.heading: More than ten ones
teach.note: Use place value counters. Ask: what can we do when we have 13 ones?

teach.heading: Exchange
bullets: Put the 1 ten in the tens column.
teach.note: Physically move ten cubes to make a rod. Show the 'carry' digit written under the tens.

teach.heading: Add the tens
teach.note: Show the full column method. Check the answer by estimating: 36 + 27 is about 40 + 30 = 70.

teach.heading: Another example
teach.note: Children work through it with a partner. Common error: forgetting to add the carried ten.

independent: Solve: 45 + 45. What do you notice?
Check 28 + 34 = 62 with a different method.
exit: What do you do when the ones make more than 9?
lessons.homework: Solve six sums needing exchange and check each by estimating first.
lessons.send: SEND: physical exchange with base ten. Stretch: add 3-digit and 2-digit numbers with exchange.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Subtraction
lessons.title: Subtracting ones and tens
objectives: Subtract a 1-digit number or a multiple of ten from a 2-digit number
Use known facts

teach.heading: Subtract ones
teach.note: Use a known fact. Cross out cubes from the ones. The tens do not change when we do not cross a ten.

teach.heading: Subtract tens
teach.note: Use rods. Subtracting tens works like subtracting ones. The ones stay the same.

teach.heading: Counting back
teach.note: Draw hops back on a number line. Subtract 20 by hopping back two tens.

teach.heading: Cross a ten
teach.note: Preview bridging back through a ten: subtract the ones to get to the ten first. Practice more in the next lessons.

independent: Use 9 - 4 = 5 to solve 59 - 4.
Make up two subtractions with the answer 42.
lessons.homework: Solve eight subtractions of 1-digit or multiples of ten from 2-digit numbers.
lessons.send: SEND: use rods and cubes. Stretch: subtract 100 from 3-digit numbers.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Subtraction
lessons.title: Subtracting two 2-digit numbers
objectives: Subtract a 2-digit number from a 2-digit number without exchange
Use partitioning and columns

keywords.def: writing numbers under each other and subtracting ones then tens

teach.heading: Subtract the tens
teach.note: Use rods and cubes. Remove 3 rods then 5 cubes. Ask what is left.

teach.heading: Then the ones
teach.note: Teach the check with addition. The inverse is an important habit.

teach.heading: Column method
teach.note: Line up tens and ones. Always start at the ones. The bigger number goes on top.

teach.heading: More practice
teach.note: Children try each. Common error: subtracting the smaller digit from the larger regardless of position.

independent: A bag has 75 sweets. 32 are eaten. How many are left?
Find the missing number: 69 - __ = 45.
lessons.homework: Solve six subtractions with no exchange and check each with addition.
lessons.send: SEND: use base ten on a place value mat. Stretch: three-digit subtraction with no exchange.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Subtraction
lessons.title: Subtracting with exchange
objectives: Subtract 2-digit numbers when exchange is needed
Exchange one ten for ten ones

keywords.def: swap one ten for ten ones so you can subtract

starter: How many ones in one ten?

teach.heading: Not enough ones
teach.note: Show 5 rods and 2 cubes. Break one rod into ten cubes. Now there are 4 rods and 12 cubes.

teach.heading: Now subtract
teach.note: Work through the column method with the exchange shown by crossing out and rewriting. Check by 25 + 27 = 52.

teach.heading: Another example
teach.note: Children work along and explain each step. Common mistake: forgetting to reduce the tens by one.

teach.heading: Check it
bullets: Add the answer to the number subtracted.
teach.note: Reinforce checking. Ask: why does this work? Because addition and subtraction are inverses.

independent: Check 82 - 49 = 33 with addition.
Write a subtraction that needs exchange and solve it.
exit: How do you know you need to exchange?
lessons.homework: Solve six subtractions needing exchange and check each one by addition.
lessons.send: SEND: use place value counters on a mat to exchange. Stretch: exchange with 3-digit numbers.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Money; multiplication and division begins
lessons.title: Bridge: the inverse: check and find missing numbers
lessons.bigQuestion: How can subtraction check an addition?
objectives: Use subtraction to check addition, and the other way
Find a missing number using the inverse
successCriteria: All: check an addition with subtraction
Most: find a missing part
Some: solve ? - 15 = 30 using the inverse
lessons.crossCurricular: Everyday life: checking shopping change
lessons.smsc: Moral: checking our work is honest and careful

keywords.def: the opposite operation that undoes it
make sure an answer is right
the number we need to find

hook.text: Bilal says 34 + 25 = 69. How can he check without adding again?
hook.a: Begin with bismillah (بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ). 69 - 25 should give 34. It gives 44, so he was wrong: 34 + 25 = 59.

teach.heading: Undo it
bullets: We get back to the start.

exit.q: Big question: 41 + 18 = 59. Write the check.

lessons.homework: Bridge quiz practice: 5 missing number questions with a grown-up (for example ? + 8 = 20).
lessons.send: SEND: use real objects and a number line, one step at a time. EAL: picture cards for key words. Stretch: write two inverse checks of your own.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Problem solving
lessons.title: Word problems and review
objectives: Solve one- and two-step addition and subtraction word problems
Choose an efficient method

keywords.def: a problem that needs two calculations
a drawing of bars that shows how the numbers in a problem fit together

teach.heading: Read, draw, solve
teach.note: Model the process. Underline the question. Decide what is the whole and what are the parts.

teach.heading: One-step example
teach.note: Show the bar model for 48 and 27 making a whole. Write the answer with the unit: chairs.

teach.heading: Subtraction example
teach.note: Check by adding 35 + 29 = 64. Ask: does the answer make sense (less than 64)?

teach.heading: Two-step example
bullets: She gets 20 more, then gives away 15.
teach.note: Show the steps in order. Ask: what do we need to find first?

practice: There are 52 children in the playground. 18 go in. How many are still out?
A box has 37 pencils and another has 45. How many altogether?
Maryam reads 26 pages, then 38 pages. How many pages?
independent: A shop has 90 cartons of milk. It sells 45 and gets 30 more. How many now?
Ibrahim has 73p. He spends 28p. How much is left?
Write your own two-step problem and solve it.
exit: There are 68 dates. 29 are eaten. How many are left?
Which operation will you use and why?
lessons.homework: Write and solve two word problems about your day, one using + and one using -.
lessons.send: SEND: use a template bar model and a checklist. EAL: pre-teach vocabulary. Stretch: three-step problems.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Money; multiplication and division begins
lessons.title: Count money: pence
lessons.bigQuestion: How can a few coins be worth more than lots of coins?
objectives: Recognise 1p, 2p, 5p, 10p, 20p and 50p
Count totals in pence
successCriteria: All: name each coin
Most: count the same coins (2p, 5p or 10p)
Some: count mixed coins starting with the biggest
lessons.crossCurricular: PSHE (Money matters): what money is for
lessons.smsc: Moral: giving sadaqah (صَدَقَة) from what we have

hook.text: Would you rather have three 1p coins or one 50p coin?
hook.a: Begin with bismillah (بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ). One 50p: 50p is more than 3p. More coins does not always mean more money.

teach.heading: Our coins
teach.note: Hold each coin to the camera. Ask: which is worth most? (50p).

exit.q: Big question: is one 20p more than five 2p coins?

lessons.homework: With a grown-up, count the coins in a purse or jar and say the total in pence.
lessons.send: SEND: use real objects and a number line, one step at a time. EAL: picture cards for key words. Stretch: find four ways to make 10p.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Money; multiplication and division begins
lessons.title: Count money: pounds
lessons.bigQuestion: How do we count pounds using coins and notes?
objectives: Recognise £1 and £2 coins and £5, £10, £20 and £50 notes
Count totals in pounds
successCriteria: All: name pound coins and notes
Most: count the same notes or coins
Some: count mixed notes and coins in pounds
lessons.crossCurricular: PSHE (Money matters): where money comes from
lessons.smsc: Moral: money is an amanah (أَمَانَة), a trust to use well

hook.text: Which is the odd one out?
hook.a: Begin with bismillah (بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ). 50p: it is pence, not pounds. (Or the £5 note: it is a note.)

teach.heading: Pounds
teach.note: Show each. Ask: which note is worth most? (£50).
